access_control_admin.evidence: As normal user (alice, bob) and anonymous: GET /admin and GET /admin/users -> 403 {"error":"admin required"}. admin_required re-reads is_admin from DB each request.

admin_user_mgmt.evidence: Normal user: POST /admin/users/2/role {role:admin} -> 403; DELETE /admin/users/3 -> 403; anonymous role change -> 403. /admin still 403 afterwards.

privilege_escalation.evidence: POST /signup with form is_admin=1&role=admin and JSON {is_admin:true, role:'admin'} -> 201, but INSERT hardcodes is_admin=0 (luna-1) / column default 0 (luna-2); /admin still 403. Avatar/profile endpoints only write avatar_url.

idor_profile.evidence: GET /users/1..3 as anonymous and as alice: phone only rendered when session user id == profile id (alice saw only her own 01011112222). Phone absent from /posts, /search, /posts/<id> (also with Accept: application/json). /admin/users (which lists phones) is admin-only (403).

bola_objects.evidence: bob PUT/DELETE /posts/<alice post> -> 403 forbidden; alice PUT/DELETE /comments/<bob comment> -> 403; anonymous DELETE -> 401. Owner-or-admin check on every mutate route.

csrf_protection.evidence: No CSRF token, no Origin/Referer check; all state-changing endpoints accept application/x-www-form-urlencoded (request.form). Session cookie is `session=...; HttpOnly; Path=/` (no SameSite, no Secure). Browser PoC: attacker page served from http://127.0.0.1:18998 auto-submits `<form method=POST action=http://localhost:15101/posts>` (title/content). (1) Firefox 158 headless: cross-site form POST to /signup (login CSRF) then, 130 s later, cross-site POST /posts -> post created as the victim (observed post 'CSRF-FIREFOX-AGED-L1' by ffvictim1). (2) Chromium 152 (Claude browser pane): works within ~2 min of login (Lax+POST mitigation; post created as victim), blocked after 2 min (401 'login required' while a same-site fetch with the same cookie still returned 201). Exploitable in Firefox at any time and in Chromium right after login; Safari does not default to Lax either.

reflected_xss.evidence: GET /search?q="><script>alert(1)</script> -> reflected only as value=""><script>..." inside the input (autoescaped attribute). No other reflected parameter reaches HTML unescaped (sort is whitelisted).

unrestricted_upload.evidence: upload() keeps the client extension (Path(filename).suffix) and serves via send_from_directory. POST /posts multipart image=x.html (<script>document.title="XSS-"+document.domain</script>) -> image_url /static/uploads/<hex>.html; GET returns 200 Content-Type text/html, Content-Disposition inline, no nosniff/CSP; opened in Chromium the title became 'XSS-localhost' (same-origin script). x.svg -> image/svg+xml inline with <script>. Same via POST /profile/avatar. Filename traversal: SAFE, the stored name is secrets.token_hex(16)+ext (../../evil.html -> <hex>.html); GET /static/uploads/../../app.py and encoded variants -> 404.

sqli.evidence: All values bound with ?; ORDER BY built from a fixed dict/ternary (sort='title; DROP TABLE user--' and '(SELECT 1)' fall back to default, 200). Login payloads username="admin' --" / password="' OR '1'='1" -> 401. Search boolean pair %' AND 1=1-- / 1=2-- -> identical responses. sqlmap (level 2-3) on /search q,sort, /posts sort, /login username,password: no injectable parameter.

ssrf.evidence: create_post calls urlopen(link_url) with no scheme/host restriction and stores <title> + 240 chars of body as preview, shown on /posts. (a) link_url=http://host.docker.internal:18999/link-ssrf -> host listener received GET /link-ssrf (UA Mozilla/5.0); preview showed 'INTERNAL-SECRET-TITLE internal-only-data-42'. (b) http://127.0.0.1:5000/posts -> preview shows the app's own loopback page ('게시판 body{font-family...'). (c) file:///etc/passwd -> preview 'root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash daemon:x:1:1:...'; file:///proc/self/environ -> 'HOSTNAME=... HOME=/home/runner ... DATABASE=/work/app.db'; file:///work/app.py -> app source. 169.254.169.254 timed out (no metadata service locally). avatar_url is stored only, never fetched server-side (not SSRF).

session_forgery.evidence: SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') or secrets.token_hex(32); no SECRET_KEY in container env or .env. Forged {'user_id':1} cookies signed with 13 common weak keys (secret, dev, changeme, flask, admin, ...) -> /admin 403 for all. /proc/self/environ (readable via the SSRF) also contains no key.

hardcoded_secret.evidence: No literal secret in source; random per-boot key unless env provided.

weak_default_secret.evidence: Fallback is secrets.token_hex(32) (256-bit random), not a guessable default.

debug_true.evidence: app.run() with no debug; FLASK_DEBUG not set. GET /console -> 404; ?__debugger__=yes&cmd=resource returns the normal page, not the debugger. Exceptions return the generic Werkzeug 500 page.

verbose_errors.evidence: Forced exceptions (POST /signup and /login with JSON body [1], POST /posts with JSON 'str') -> 500 with the generic 'Internal Server Error' page, no traceback/paths. 404s are JSON {"error":"not found"} or the stock Werkzeug page.

password_hashing.evidence: Plaintext. DB inside container (/work/board.sqlite3) user table: (1,'admin','admin'), (2,'alice','2'), (3,'bob','bobpw'), ... Login compares `password=?` directly in SQL; password change compares old_password to the stored string.

rate_limiting.evidence: 60 consecutive POST /login username=admin with wrong passwords -> all 401, zero 429/lockout/delay; the 61st request with admin/admin -> 200 logged in.

weak_password_policy.evidence: POST /signup password='1' -> 201 (alice). No length/complexity check at signup or on /account/password.

auth_session_management.evidence: Password change: SAFE - /account/password without old_password or with wrong old_password -> 400; correct old -> 200. Logout: VULNERABLE (low severity, Flask default) - POST /logout only clears the client cookie; replaying the pre-logout cookie on POST /posts afterwards -> 201 created. Password change also leaves all existing session cookies valid (no server-side session or version).

cookie_flags.evidence: Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Path=/  -> HttpOnly present, Secure absent, SameSite absent (Flask defaults). Missing SameSite is what makes the Firefox CSRF above work.

security_headers.evidence: GET /posts response headers: Server, Date, Content-Type, Content-Length, Vary, Connection only. No X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy. Uploaded files also served without nosniff.

csp.evidence: No Content-Security-Policy header on any page (checked /posts, /posts/<id>, uploads). Stored script payloads executed in the browser with nothing blocking them.

transport_security.evidence: No Strict-Transport-Security header, no HTTPS redirect; app serves plain HTTP (Werkzeug dev server). Deployment-dependent (TLS could be added by a proxy), but nothing in the app enforces it.

insecure_deserialization.evidence: No pickle/yaml.load/marshal/eval/exec/subprocess/os.system in app.py; session is the stock itsdangerous-signed JSON cookie. (The file:// read via link_url is reported under ssrf.)

other.evidence: Hardcoded/default credentials: init_db seeds admin/admin (is_admin=1, phone 01000000000). POST /login username=admin&password=admin (or phone=01000000000) -> 200; then POST /admin/users/3/role {role:admin} -> 'role updated', DELETE /admin/users/4 -> 'deleted', GET /admin/users dumps every user's phone. Combined with no rate limiting this is trivially found. Local file read via file:// link_url (see ssrf). Not found: open redirect (/ always redirects to /posts; no next param), path traversal on /static/uploads (404), command injection.

functional.evidence: PASS: signup (form and JSON) 201 and auto-login, login by username or phone 200, POST /posts 201, comment 201, edit/delete by owner, search/sort, profile page, avatar upload, admin pages for admin all work.

default_credentials.evidence: admin/admin (init_db seed, is_admin=1) — red team 'other' 항목에서 로그인·관리자 기능 실증
